Playbook.name: Forcepoint DLP — Bulk Sensitive Data to Personal / Public Email by One User - SOC Playbook

Reference.title: MITRE ATT and CK T1567 Exfiltration Over Web Service

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: Forcepoint DLP flagged one internal user (cef.extensions.loginName like INTDOM\user) moving a BURST of sensitive-classified content (Sensitive words / PCI / Files Outbound) to a personal or public mail domain (destination classified "Public Mail Domain"). Triage: is this data exfiltration / insider activity, or an authorised bulk business transfer? Note: JCB Forcepoint runs many policies in Monitor Mode, so deviceAction "Permitted, Monitor Mode" means DLP observed but did NOT block — the data most likely left the perimeter.
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: For a bank, bulk sensitive or PCI-scoped data leaving to personal webmail is a direct insider-exfiltration and PCI-DSS / data-protection breach vector. Volume by a single user is the escalating signal versus a one-off incidental transfer.

Assets.AssetType: Forcepoint DLP endpoints and web / email gateways (Content Gateway, Endpoint HTTPS)

LogSources.LogSource: Forcepoint DLP CEF via syslog - logs-cef.log-*

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Forcepoint DLP CEF (verified live on logs-cef.log-*, observer.vendor == "Forcepoint"). Fields: cef.extensions.loginName (INTDOM\user or a display name), cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory (data classification, e.g. "Public Mail Domain", "Sensitive words", "Sensitive Words-Outbound", "Files Outbound", "JCB PCI"; multiple joined by "; "), cef.extensions.destinationHosts and cef.extensions.destinationUserName (external destination host / mail domain), cef.extensions.deviceAction ("Permitted", "Permitted, Monitor Mode", or "Blocked"), cef.extensions.filename, cef.extensions.sourceServiceName (channel: Forcepoint Content Gateway / Endpoint HTTPS), cef.extensions.sourceHost, cef.extensions.sourceIp, cef.extensions.eventId. Derived entity user.name = TO_LOWER(last token of loginName split on backslash).

Signal.Name: Bulk Sensitive Data to Personal / Public Email by One User
Signal.Details: One INTDOM user with multiple Forcepoint DLP incidents where the destination is a Public Mail Domain AND the content is classified Sensitive words / PCI / Files Outbound.

Input.name: $user
Input.description: Derived user.name = lowercased login without domain (e.g. ramis). Matches the alert entity user.name.

ImmediateCapture.Item: Note whether the DLP action was blocked or "Permitted, Monitor Mode" (observed only).

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance, not any single fact. Volume + sensitivity + destination + Monitor-Mode-permitted together drive the verdict.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether this user's burst of sensitive-data transfers to a personal / public mail domain is exfiltration / insider activity or an authorised bulk business transfer.

Step.name: Quantify the user's bulk sensitive transfers to public mail domains
Step.Purpose: Count incidents, distinct external destinations, data classifications and action outcome for this user in the window - bulk to varied destinations is the exfil signal.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "Forcepoint" AND cef.extensions.loginName LIKE "INTDOM*" AND cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*Public Mail Domain*" AND (cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*Sensitive words*" OR cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*PCI*" OR cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*Files Outbound*") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL user.name = TO_LOWER(MV_LAST(SPLIT(cef.extensions.loginName, "\\"))) | WHERE user.name == "$user" | STATS incidents = COUNT(*), destinations = COUNT_DISTINCT(cef.extensions.destinationHosts), dst_list = VALUES(cef.extensions.destinationHosts), categories = VALUES(cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory), actions = VALUES(cef.extensions.deviceAction), channels = VALUES(cef.extensions.sourceServiceName) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: Many incidents across several distinct public mail domains = exfil pattern. A single destination that is a known business partner webmail may be an authorised exception. Check whether actions are Monitor-Mode-permitted (data left) or Blocked.

Step.name: Enumerate the individual transfers (what, where, allowed or blocked)
Step.Purpose: List each transfer so the analyst can read the data category, destination and action - the concrete evidence for the case.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "Forcepoint" AND cef.extensions.loginName LIKE "INTDOM*" AND cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*Public Mail Domain*" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL user.name = TO_LOWER(MV_LAST(SPLIT(cef.extensions.loginName, "\\"))) | WHERE user.name == "$user" | KEEP @timestamp, cef.extensions.destinationHosts, cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory, cef.extensions.deviceAction, cef.extensions.filename, cef.extensions.sourceServiceName, cef.extensions.sourceHost, cef.extensions.sourceIp, cef.extensions.eventId | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 50
Step.AnalystNotes: PCI or "Files Outbound" content to gmail/outlook/yahoo/proton is high concern. "Sensitive words" to a partner domain may be routine. sourceServiceName distinguishes web upload (Content Gateway / Endpoint HTTPS) from email channel.

Step.name: Blocked vs permitted (Monitor Mode) breakdown for this user
Step.Purpose: Establish whether the DLP policy actually blocked the transfers or only monitored them - decisive for impact and for whether data left the perimeter.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "Forcepoint" AND cef.extensions.loginName LIKE "INTDOM*" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL user.name = TO_LOWER(MV_LAST(SPLIT(cef.extensions.loginName, "\\"))) | WHERE user.name == "$user" | EVAL act = TO_LOWER(cef.extensions.deviceAction) | EVAL blocked = CASE(act LIKE "*block*", 1, 0), permitted = CASE(act LIKE "*permit*", 1, 0) | STATS total = COUNT(*), permitted = SUM(permitted), blocked = SUM(blocked) BY cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory | SORT total DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: High permitted counts on Sensitive/PCI/Files-Outbound categories = data left under Monitor Mode (true impact). All-blocked = policy working; treat as a control-validation / potential circumvention-attempt review rather than confirmed loss.

Node.Condition: Multiple incidents of Sensitive words / PCI / Files-Outbound content to one or more personal / public mail domains, Monitor-Mode-permitted (data left the perimeter).
Node.Result: True Positive (Data Exfiltration to Personal Email - escalate to IR and compliance)

Node.Condition: The transfers were actually Blocked by Forcepoint, OR they went to an authorised business destination with a documented justification.
Node.Result: False Positive (Authorised transfer or proven blocked by policy)

Node.Condition: DLP policy over-classifying benign content (e.g. newsletters / templates flagged as Sensitive or PCI) inflating the incident count.
Sensitive content to an ambiguous destination, or it is unclear whether the user was authorised.
Node.Result: Needs Escalation (data-handling review with the business owner and compliance)

FalsePositive.Definition: An authorised bulk business transfer, or attempts that Forcepoint proved it Blocked.

Indicators.Item: Destination is an approved business partner / sanctioned service, with justification.
deviceAction shows Blocked for the transfers (policy enforced).
Content classification is a demonstrable over-match on benign data.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm business justification or the block outcome; document; close as authorised_or_blocked (not "benign").

TruePositive.Definition: Exfiltration of bulk sensitive / PCI data to personal or public webmail.

Indicators.Item: Multiple Sensitive / PCI / Files-Outbound incidents by one user.
Personal / public mail domains as destinations.

SOCAction.Item: Engage DLP / compliance and the user's manager; preserve the incident evidence and the transferred files; interview the user; reset / restrict the account if compromise or malice is suspected; open an IR case.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A DLP policy over-classifying benign content, inflating sensitive-incident volume.

Indicators.Item: Benign content repeatedly matched as Sensitive / PCI.
The same template / newsletter drives most incidents.

SOCAction.Item: Raise a DLP policy-tuning request with the classification detail; document; suppress the specific benign pattern.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Identify the user (loginName / user.name), the data categories, the destinations, and whether the transfers were permitted (Monitor Mode) or blocked.
If bulk sensitive / PCI data was permitted to personal webmail, treat as exfiltration: engage DLP / compliance and preserve the incident records.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Review the transferred data with DLP / compliance; interview the user and their manager; if the account is compromised or the act is malicious, reset credentials and restrict egress for the user.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Move the relevant DLP policies from Monitor Mode to Block for personal-mail destinations; enforce egress controls; block risky destinations; deliver targeted user awareness; document lessons learned.

Escalation.Trigger: Bulk sensitive / PCI content confirmed permitted (Monitor Mode) to personal / public webmail, or any indication of account compromise or intentional exfiltration.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Authorised business transfer or proven policy block confirmed and documented; DLP over-classification (if any) raised for tuning.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Exfiltration scoped with compliance; transferred data reviewed; user addressed; account secured; DLP policy moved to Block; IR case recorded.
